purpose: Osilodrostat is used to treat adults with Cushing's disease, a condition where the body makes too much of a stress hormone called cortisol. It is typically used when surgery has not worked or is not an option. Keeping cortisol levels under control helps reduce symptoms like weight gain, high blood pressure, and muscle weakness.
how_it_works: Your body makes cortisol in the adrenal glands, which sit on top of your kidneys. Osilodrostat works by blocking a key enzyme called 11-beta-hydroxylase that your body needs to produce cortisol. By blocking this enzyme, the medication lowers the amount of cortisol your body makes, bringing levels back toward normal.
common_side_effects: Common side effects include nausea, headache, fatigue, low cortisol levels (which can cause dizziness, weakness, or nausea), swelling, vomiting, skin darkening, and joint pain. Some people may also notice changes in hormone levels that can cause acne or unwanted hair growth in women.
warnings: This medicine can cause cortisol levels to drop too low (adrenal insufficiency), which can be life-threatening — watch for extreme tiredness, dizziness, or fainting and contact your doctor right away. It can also affect heart rhythm (QT prolongation), so tell your doctor if you have any heart conditions. It may cause hormonal imbalances and should not be used during pregnancy. Regular blood tests and monitoring are very important while taking this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 2 mg taken by mouth twice a day (morning and evening). Your doctor will adjust your dose based on your cortisol levels, typically every few weeks, up to a maximum of 30 mg twice daily. It can be taken with or without food.
